sentences.text: This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:

ORDER Applicant has filed this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 on behalf of the applicant for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.154/2023 registered at P.S. Neemuch Cantt., District Neemuch (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC.
He is in jail since 12.04.2023.
2. As per the prosecution story, on 18.03.2023, present applicant/ accused took away the victim on motorcycle and the incident was seen by mother of the victim.
She tried to call her back, but accused ran away from there and took her daughter to a Hotel and there committed rape upon her.

Accordingly, a case has been registered against the present applicant.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
Applicant is in jail since 12.04.2023.

Investigation is over and Aadil @ Sameer Mansuri vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134022422/

sentences.text: charge-sheet has been filed.
Prosecutrix is major lady.
Prosecutrix and present applicant were in love affair and they have got married with their own consent.
Marriage Certificate/ Nikahnama is also executed in the presence of Kazi.

Prosecutrix in her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
contended that their marriage was solemnized in presence of parents of applicant .
Medical evidence is not corroborating the prosecution story.
Applicant is a permanent resident of District Neemuch and is sole bread earner of his family.
Final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
Hence, he prays that applicant be released on bail.

4. Per-contra, learned counsel for respondent/State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
corroborated the FIR.
Hence, he prays that present applicant does not deserve for bail.

5. Perused the case diary as well as the impugned order of the court below.
6.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, nature and gravity of allegation as also taking note of the fact that applicant and prosecutrix both are major and they were having love affair; from perusal of Nikahnama, it reveals that they have solemnized their marriage; prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
also stated that she has solemnized her marriage with the present applicant with her own consent;
investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed and final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
7.
In view of the above, without commenting on the merits of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
8. Accordingly, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3)
Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

( ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Anushree Aadil @ Sameer Mansuri vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134022422/
